evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 形義通解: formation and semantic development
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 本 as 木 plus 一, with the mark indicating the lower part of a plant; it gives the original sense as plant root. It cites 說文解字 and 呂氏春秋·辯土 (with Gao You's note “本，根也”), then records extensions to the base/end of an elongated object, a tree trunk, a foundation or principal part, source/cause, basis/evidence, manuscript draft, and a classifier. These are dictionary-supported historical uses, not a dated chronology proving each transition.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 本

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.field: 字形資料 and 說文/廣韻 records
evidence.text: The page displays one small-seal form, seven manuscript forms, and one other form, while its 金文 and 甲骨 slots show no displayed examples. It gives the Shuowen entry: “木下曰本。从木，一在其下。…楍，古文。” and Guangyun fanqie 布忖. The absence of displayed oracle/bronze forms is a database display fact, not by itself proof that no such forms exist.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 本

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: The entry distinguishes two transmitted Shuowen readings: the Daxu text analyzes 木 plus 一 below it; Duan Yucai's annotated text instead reads 木 plus 丅. It also notes that 夲 has an independent sense/pronunciation (tāo, rapid advance) although it has also served as a popular written variant of 本. This establishes competing textual/form analyses and variant use, not a chronological ancestor relationship between 本 and 夲.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》 — 本

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 釋義: senses with cited texts
evidence.text: The dictionary cites 詩經·大雅·蕩 “枝葉未有害，本實先撥” for a plant's lower part/root; 莊子·逍遙遊 for trunk; 書經·五子之歌 and 論語·學而 for foundation; and later cited texts for ancestor, source, original/innate, basis, agriculture, capital, principal, current, books and classifiers. Its sense list documents examples and cited works, but should not be read as a lexical chronology.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education 《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》 — 本

evidence.source: Du Qingyu (杜清雨), Lingnan Journal of Chinese Studies
evidence.text: A 2025 article argues that a disputed oracle-bone graph is an early form of 本 and interprets it in sacrificial inscriptions as a human torso or lower body, possibly connected with dismemberment or waist execution. Its abstract reports other identifications as 垂, 叕, and 瓜 and argues they have shortcomings. This is a recent disputed proposal, not settled evidence that the received tree-root graph is attested in oracle-bone writing.
evidence.title: 甲骨文“本”字試解 / An explanation of the character in Oracle Bone Inscription

evidence.source: 漢字教育士ひろりんの書斎
evidence.field: 2018 discussion: early attestation and competing structure
evidence.text: The author reports finding no oracle-bone 本 in the references checked and only a rare Western Zhou bronze example on the vessel called 本鼎; the author treats it as likely a maker's name, so its word meaning is uncertain. The article notes the transmitted Shuowen analysis 木 plus 一, contrasted with Duan Yucai's 木 plus the seal form of 下, and reports that both readings give a lower/tree-related meaning. This is a secondary discussion and an explicit challenge to treating the bronze graph as secure semantic evidence.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.source: 漢字教育士ひろりんの書斎, quoting 詩經 and 論語
evidence.text: The page quotes 詩經·大雅·蕩 “枝葉未有害，本實先撥” and explains 本 as root in context; it also quotes 論語·學而 “君子務本，本立而道生” in a foundation sense. These are transmitted-text attestations, not archaeological inscriptions. The page does not establish exact composition dates for the passages, so no precise earliest date is assigned here.
evidence.title: 本という字の謎

evidence.text: The entry gives modern Standard Mandarin běn (Pinyin), Cantonese bun2 (Jyutping, Guangzhou–Hong Kong), Middle Chinese pwonX (Baxter notation; also gives Guangyun fanqie 布忖), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *C.pˤə[n]ʔ, and Zhengzhang Shangfang *pɯːnʔ. These are readings/reconstructions of 本, not of 木 or 一 as a proposed phonetic element. They support a descriptive sound history for 本 but do not make either component phonetic.
evidence.title: 本 - Wiktionary

evidence.field: Historical lexical examples and modern reading
evidence.text: The entry gives běn and quotes Shuowen “木下曰本,” 呂氏春秋·士容論·辯士 with Han commentator Gao You glossing 本 as root, and 論語·學而 “君子務本，本立而道生.” It separately lists book/document, capital, manuscript, basis, original, current, and self/own-side uses. gaps: No glyph image was visually inspected. The CUHK record displays a small-seal image but no bronze/oracle examples; the Japanese discussion reports no oracle form and questions whether the rare Western Zhou 本鼎 graph is the same word, while a 2025 scholarly article proposes a disputed oracle-bone precursor. The competing palaeographic analyses remain unresolved.

The mark 一 is a semantic indicator in the standard accounts, not a phonetic component; 木 is likewise described semantically. No phonetic-series analysis or component-specific pronunciation comparison is supported by the inspected sources.

No independent sound evidence was found establishing a Proto-Sino-Tibetan etymology for the word 本 from the cited reconstruction proposal. The dossier's cognate proposal is not independently verified here, and the inspected source data only establish Chinese readings/reconstructions.

Literary examples survive in named transmitted works, but this research did not independently establish their composition dates. Dictionary sense order is not used to infer a chronology of semantic extensions.

The Han commentator's root gloss and later dictionary examples document root, trunk, base/foundation, source, basis, and other uses, but the semantic pathways and first occurrence dates for abstract, documentary, financial, and classifier senses remain unestablished.
Chinese Text Project pages returned HTTP 403 on direct opening. Search-result snippets were recorded as access-limited leads and not treated as opened evidence.
